what: R5 warp-net training rule (PLAN 10.8; fills in r5_train_plan's warp clause, sha 6aadb964...). Sealed 2026-11-03 before any R5 warp training and before the R5 segmenter finished (its chain is still waiting for the IXI charm queue): no R5 model or R5 result exists.
setting: head-model commit ca8c945: scripts/r5_warp.py and scripts/train_r5_warp.sh. Labels: every head of Dataset602's 5-fold split predicted by the one fold that held it out, through navprep's own segment stage (LPS 1 mm grid, crop, nnU-Net with mirroring, largest connected part, charm labels), on the case's charm input T1; the warp input is that conformed T1 and those labels, our raw affine computed from them (warpnet.cache_case, template runs/wp3b/template_trainminusval); the target is charm's own MNI map of the case. Train = round 1's train cases minus the 30 WP3b validation cases + the IXI train heads of r5_ixi_split; validation = the 30 WP3b validation cases + the 30 IXI validation heads (r5_warp.sets). Model: warpnet NetConfig defaults (round 3's U-Net). TrainConfig defaults (round 3's lr, schedule, augmentation, w_diff) except: w_tail 1.0 (as round 3), w_gate 4.0, val_every 20, max_hours 30 per run. w_gate: the 27 gated points of wp3_gate_rtms_set (10 targets, the 13 rTMS electrodes including Cz, the 4 fiducials Nz Iz LPA RPA) weigh 4, the other 63 points 1, so the gated points carry 108/171 = 63 % of the point loss; the value is fixed here, not tuned. At inference: register.adopted_setting() with this net as init_warp (round 4's SVF refinement, fill and unfold), via HM_WARP_NET.
epochs: Epoch pilot (user rule 2026-10-28: pilot every training on the first 5 validation cases): two runs, 100 and 200 epochs, each a full cosine schedule, scored by r5_warp.py score on the first 5 sorted validation heads (score_gate = mean of targets mean, rTMS EEG set mean, fiducial mean; unprojected, subject mm). gain = score_100 - score_200. Final length: 200 epochs if gain < 0.03 mm, 350 if gain < 0.10 mm, else 500. Why these lengths: R5 has about 4.4x round 3's 111 training heads, so 200 R5 epochs are about 880 round-3 epochs in samples seen (round 3 chose 1000). The model is the final run's last.pt (not the best on validation), its training support stored in it (r5_warp.py finalise), linked as runs/r5/warp/final.
rule: Nothing here changes after any R5 warp result is seen, except by a new sealed amendment that says why. This rule only trains; whether R5 replaces the release is decided by the end-to-end rule r5_e2e alone.
no_folding: not judged here (training only); r5_e2e requires written-map min Jacobian > 0 in both maps on every test case of R5's 1 mm arm.
disclosure: Before sealing, the code was smoke-tested on Dataset699 (6 IXI training heads, a 1-epoch segmenter, a 2-epoch warp on 1 head, scratch directory): machinery only, numbers meaningless (targets ~18 mm). The round-3 net's results on the WP3b validation cases are known (rule wp3b_r3_adopt). No IXI validation or test head has been scored by any warp net.
